description: Le vocabulaire de la cellule, des moteurs, des circuits, du train et de l'avionique, pour décrire une panne avec le mot juste.

fiches.question: A hinged surface on the trailing edge of each wing that controls roll.
fiches.explication: The left aileron is jammed, we have limited roll control.

fiches.question: The movable surface on the horizontal tail that controls pitch.
fiches.explication: We suspect damage to the elevator after the hard landing.

fiches.question: The movable surface on the vertical fin that controls yaw.
fiches.explication: We have a rudder travel limiter fault.

fiches.question: Panels on the trailing edge of the wing, extended to increase lift and drag for take-off and landing.
fiches.explication: We have a flap asymmetry and will land with flaps up.

fiches.question: Movable panels on the leading edge of the wing that allow a higher angle of attack at low speed.
fiches.explication: The slats are stuck, we need a longer runway.

fiches.question: Panels on the upper surface of the wing, raised to reduce lift and increase drag.
fiches.explication: The spoilers did not deploy on touchdown.

fiches.question: A small adjustment of a control surface that removes the need to hold pressure on the controls.
fiches.explication: We have a stabiliser trim runaway.

fiches.question: The main body of the aircraft.
fiches.explication: A cabin crew member reports a loud noise from the rear fuselage.

fiches.question: The front edge of a wing.
fiches.explication: We may have damage to the leading edge after a bird strike.

fiches.question: The rear edge of a wing.
fiches.explication: Ground staff saw a panel hanging from the trailing edge.

fiches.question: The fixed horizontal surface of the tail.
fiches.explication: Ice on the horizontal stabiliser can cause a tailplane stall.

fiches.question: The fixed vertical surface of the tail.
fiches.explication: The fin was hit by lightning.

fiches.question: The upturned tip of a wing that reduces drag.
fiches.explication: A catering truck damaged the left winglet.

fiches.question: The small control stick at the side of the pilot's seat, used instead of a control column on fly-by-wire aircraft.
fiches.explication: Both sidesticks were moved at the same time: dual input.

fiches.question: A flight control system in which pilot inputs are sent as electrical signals to computers that move the control surfaces.
fiches.explication: On a fly-by-wire aircraft, the computers protect the flight envelope.

fiches.question: Stuck and unable to move.
fiches.explication: The elevator is jammed, we are using trim to control pitch.

fiches.question: The front window of the cockpit.
fiches.explication: We have a cracked windscreen and will descend as a precaution.

fiches.question: The compartment under the cabin floor where baggage and freight are carried.
fiches.explication: We have a smoke warning in the forward cargo hold.

fiches.question: The forward force produced by an engine.
fiches.explication: Engine one is not producing any thrust.

fiches.question: A device that redirects engine thrust forwards to slow the aircraft after landing.
fiches.explication: The left thrust reverser is locked out.

fiches.question: The unintended loss of combustion in a jet engine, so that the engine stops running.
fiches.explication: Engine two flamed out in heavy rain.

fiches.question: A breakdown of airflow through the compressor, often with loud bangs and flames from the exhaust.
fiches.explication: Passengers heard bangs and saw flames: probably an engine surge.

fiches.question: (Of an engine) to stop suddenly because its moving parts lock together.
fiches.explication: The engine seized after the oil pressure dropped to zero.

fiches.question: To stop an engine deliberately.
fiches.explication: We shut down engine one as a precaution.

fiches.question: A loss of fuel through a hole or a faulty seal.
fiches.explication: We suspect a fuel leak from the right wing.

fiches.question: A difference in fuel quantity between the left and right tanks.
fiches.explication: We are correcting a fuel imbalance with the crossfeed.

fiches.question: A valve system that lets the tank on one side supply the engine on the other side.
fiches.explication: Open the crossfeed valve to balance the fuel.

fiches.question: Releasing fuel in flight to reduce the landing weight.
fiches.explication: Request a block of airspace for fuel jettison.

fiches.question: A message telling ATC that any change to the clearance may leave the aircraft with less than its final reserve fuel; it is not yet an emergency.
fiches.explication: Minimum fuel, we can accept no further delay.

fiches.question: A small turbine, usually in the tail, that supplies electrical power and bleed air.
fiches.explication: We will start the APU as a backup for the generator.

fiches.question: To restart an engine in flight after a flameout.
fiches.explication: We managed to relight engine two at flight level 200.

fiches.question: The temperature of the gases leaving the engine, a key indicator of engine health.
fiches.explication: The EGT exceeded the limit during the start.

fiches.question: A container of extinguishing agent discharged into an engine or the APU in case of fire.
fiches.explication: We discharged both fire bottles, the warning is still on.

fiches.question: The lowest engine power setting.
fiches.explication: The engine is stuck at idle.

fiches.question: An engine stopping because fuel cannot reach it, although there is fuel on board.
fiches.explication: The investigation found fuel starvation, not a lack of fuel.

fiches.question: The aircraft having no usable fuel left at all.
fiches.explication: Fuel exhaustion led to a glide to the nearest field.

fiches.question: (Of a jet engine) to accelerate to a higher speed.
fiches.explication: The engines take a few seconds to spool up after you advance the thrust levers.

fiches.question: A device that moves a control surface or a component using hydraulic or electric power.
fiches.explication: The flap actuator has failed.

fiches.question: A container that stores hydraulic fluid under pressure as a short reserve.
fiches.explication: The brake accumulator gives us a few applications of the parking brake.

fiches.question: A small propeller that drops into the airflow to provide emergency hydraulic or electrical power.
fiches.explication: The ram air turbine deployed after the dual engine failure.

fiches.question: A machine driven by an engine that produces electrical power.
fiches.explication: We have lost generator two.

fiches.question: A distribution point that feeds electrical power to a group of systems.
fiches.explication: The essential bus is powered by the battery.

fiches.question: A switch that cuts a circuit automatically when the current is too high.
fiches.explication: The circuit breaker popped and we reset it once.

fiches.question: An unwanted connection that lets current flow where it should not, often causing heat or smoke.
fiches.explication: A short circuit in the galley caused the smell of burning.

fiches.question: Hot compressed air taken from the engines for air conditioning, pressurisation and anti-icing.
fiches.explication: We have a bleed air leak in the left wing.

fiches.question: An air conditioning unit that cools bleed air before it enters the cabin.
fiches.explication: With one pack inoperative we must stay below flight level 310.

fiches.question: A tube or channel that carries air through the aircraft.
fiches.explication: A hot air duct has burst behind the cargo lining.

fiches.question: A temperature higher than the safe limit.
fiches.explication: We have a bleed duct overheat warning.

fiches.question: Switching off non-essential electrical equipment to reduce the demand on a generator.
fiches.explication: Load shedding switched off the galleys and the in-flight entertainment.

fiches.question: The use of duplicate systems so that a single failure does not cause a loss of function.
fiches.explication: There is enough redundancy to continue to destination.

fiches.question: A device that converts direct current into alternating current.
fiches.explication: The static inverter supplies AC power from the battery.

fiches.question: Flying the aircraft without powered assistance, through cables or mechanical links.
fiches.explication: With all hydraulics lost, the crew flew in manual reversion.

fiches.question: A defect in a system or a component.
fiches.explication: We have a hydraulic fault and need to check the landing distance.

fiches.question: Happening from time to time, not continuously.
fiches.explication: We have an intermittent generator fault.

fiches.question: The wheels, struts and associated parts that support the aircraft on the ground.
fiches.explication: The landing gear will not retract.

fiches.question: The system that turns the nose wheel to steer on the ground.
fiches.explication: We have lost nose wheel steering and need a tow from the runway.

fiches.question: The mechanism that holds the landing gear in the extended position.
fiches.explication: We have no downlock indication on the left main gear.

fiches.question: Lowering the landing gear by letting it fall under its own weight when the normal system fails.
fiches.explication: We will try a gravity extension of the gear.

fiches.question: A tyre that has burst.
fiches.explication: We had a blown tyre on take-off, please inspect the runway.

fiches.question: Brakes that have overheated, for example after a rejected take-off.
fiches.explication: We have hot brakes, keep the fire services nearby.

fiches.question: A system that prevents the wheels from locking during braking.
fiches.explication: Anti-skid is inoperative, braking will be more difficult.

fiches.question: A system that applies the brakes automatically at a preselected rate after touchdown.
fiches.explication: Set autobrake to medium for the wet runway.

fiches.question: Stopping the aircraft on the runway after the take-off run has started.
fiches.explication: We performed a rejected take-off at 120 knots.

fiches.question: The part of the landing gear that absorbs the impact of landing.
fiches.explication: The left shock absorber looks compressed.

fiches.question: The space in the wing or fuselage where a retracted wheel is stowed.
fiches.explication: A stowaway was found in the wheel well.

fiches.question: Panels that close over the landing gear once it is retracted.
fiches.explication: The gear doors did not close, we will keep the speed low.

fiches.question: A landing with the landing gear retracted, on the underside of the fuselage.
fiches.explication: The crew made a belly landing on a foamed runway.

fiches.question: A plug in a wheel that melts at high temperature to let the tyre deflate before it bursts.
fiches.explication: The fusible plugs melted after the hot brake event.

fiches.question: Moving the aircraft backwards away from the gate with a tug.
fiches.explication: Request pushback and start-up.

fiches.question: A bar connecting a tug to the nose wheel to move the aircraft.
fiches.explication: The towbar sheared during the pushback.

fiches.question: Wedges placed against the wheels to stop the aircraft from moving.
fiches.explication: Chocks are in, you can release the parking brake.

fiches.question: The pressure inside the cabin, expressed as an equivalent altitude.
fiches.explication: The cabin altitude is climbing through 10,000 feet.

fiches.question: The valve that controls cabin pressure by letting air out of the fuselage.
fiches.explication: The outflow valve is stuck open.

fiches.question: A sudden loss of cabin pressure.
fiches.explication: We have a rapid decompression and are starting an emergency descent.

fiches.question: A fast descent to a safe altitude after a loss of pressurisation.
fiches.explication: Emergency descent to flight level 100, turning right off the airway.

fiches.question: A lack of oxygen in the body, which affects judgement before the person notices it.
fiches.explication: One sign of hypoxia is a feeling of well-being.

fiches.question: The time a person can still act effectively after the oxygen supply is lost.
fiches.explication: At flight level 400, the time of useful consciousness is only a few seconds.

fiches.question: To switch off a system such as the autopilot.
fiches.explication: The autopilot disengaged on its own.

fiches.question: The computer that manages navigation, performance and the route.
fiches.explication: Both flight management systems have failed, we need radar vectors.

fiches.question: The equipment that replies to radar signals with the aircraft's code and altitude.
fiches.explication: Our transponder seems to have failed.

fiches.question: To set a code on the transponder.
fiches.explication: Squawk 7700.

fiches.question: A TCAS instruction to climb or descend to avoid a collision.
fiches.explication: We are climbing in response to a TCAS resolution advisory.

fiches.question: An alert warning the crew that the aircraft is dangerously close to the ground.
fiches.explication: We had a ground proximity warning and went around.

fiches.question: A probe facing the airflow that measures airspeed.
fiches.explication: We suspect blocked pitot tubes.

fiches.question: A situation in which the speed indications cannot be trusted.
fiches.explication: We have unreliable airspeed, request a block altitude.

fiches.question: A small hole on the side of the fuselage that measures the outside air pressure.
fiches.explication: Tape left over the static ports caused false altitude readings.

fiches.question: (Of a display) showing nothing at all.
fiches.explication: Both displays went blank for a few seconds.

fiches.question: (Of a light or a display) to go on and off quickly.
fiches.explication: The cockpit lights are flickering.
